Here we investigate the role of gravity in supercooled FOPTs that occur in the RSB scenario. We use a model-independent approach that is valid when a quantity (which we explicitly determine and is computable once the model is specified) is small enough. Eventually, the curvature of spacetime becomes relevant if the FOPT does not complete in the case in which gravity is ignored. We also include the effect on the FOPT of the non-minimal couplings with coefficients of zero mass dimension. Depending on such non-minimal couplings, gravity can enhance or reduce the region of parameter space where the phase transition completes. Observable consequences of the role of gravity on the FOPT that can be probed by current and future GW detectors are then worked out and we explore the possibility that the background of GWs detected by pulsar timing arrays is produced by FOPTs in the RSB scenario. We also estimate the number of e-folds that elapse when the field playing the role of the order parameter is trapped in the false vacuum, which provides important information for cosmology.

hep-th.title: Separation of variables for massive spin-2 fields on the Kerr black hole
hep-th.author: Oscar J.C. Dias, Jorge E. Santos
hep-th.abstract: Massive spin-2 fields on the Kerr black hole generally obey coupled partial differential equations. We show that these equations separate through two commuting angular operators acting on five components of the field, its curl and its linearised Weyl tensor. A joint angular eigenfunction fixes the relative profiles of the five polarisations and leaves one second-order radial equation. The separation constants satisfy an algebraic relation that follows from the angular operators themselves. The construction removes the obstruction to a Teukolsky-type equation by a radial transport identity, then eliminates the additional radial solution through a first integral. It provides ordinary differential equations for massive spin-2 fields on Kerr, and, equivalently, for Kaluza-Klein perturbations of the Kerr black string.

hep-th.title: Relating approaches to interacting quantum clocks and systems
hep-th.author: Artur Semião, Leonardo Chataignier
hep-th.abstract: The problem of describing the dynamics of quantum systems relative to quantum clocks with which they interact is relevant to the physics of quantum reference frames and quantum gravity alike. There have been different approaches that derive a relational time-dependent Schrödinger equation for the system relative to the clock from a time-independent Hamiltonian constraint. We show that some of these approaches, due to Smith and Ahmadi, Gemsheim and Rost, as well as the so-called Born-Oppenheimer approach, can be unified in a single framework for describing conditional quantum states. In particular, the Born-Oppenheimer approach to quantum cosmology is seen to correspond to a type of interacting Page-Wootters formalism. We discuss the issue of unitarity and linearity, or lack thereof, in the relational dynamics, and we conclude with a brief outlook to further developments.

hep-th.title: Bounds on the minimum orbital period of general static spherical black holes: a sharp upper bound and a conditional lower bound
hep-th.author: Yan Peng, Guohua Liu
hep-th.abstract: We investigate bounds on the minimum orbital period around four-dimensional general static spherical black holes. For all static spherically symmetric black holes with an event horizon, asymptotic flatness and non-negative energy density outside the horizon, we prove $T_{\min}\leq 6\sqrt{3}\,\pi M$. The bound is sharp and is saturated by the Schwarzschild solution. The lower bound requires an additional condition on the exterior matter: under the tangential pressure condition $p_{\tau}\geq(\kappa/2)\rho$ with $\kappa>1$, imposed for all $r\geq r_{g}$, where $r_{g}$ is the largest radius at which $T(r)$ attains its global minimum, we prove $T_{\min}\geq c(\kappa)M$ with $c(\kappa)=6\sqrt{3}\pi(\kappa-1)\sqrt{\kappa+2}/\kappa^{3/2}$. In summary, both bounds apply to the same geometric class and differ only in what they demand of the matter: non-negative energy density suffices for the upper bound, while the lower bound is established under the additional tangential pressure condition.

hep-th.title: A systematic study of hydrodynamic attractors in periodically driven systems at weak and strong couplings
hep-th.author: Aleksas Mazeliauskas, Toshali Mitra, Sören Schlichting, Simon Schneider, Louis Nwakile Onwuka, Martin Vrdoljak
hep-th.abstract: We study equilibration and hydrodynamic response in conformal systems undergoing periodic expansion and contraction along one spatial direction. Using strongly coupled holography (AdS/CFT), weakly coupled kinetic theories (relaxation-time approximation, scalar $\phi^4$ theory and the Yang--Mills sector of QCD effective kinetic theory) and hydrodynamics (Navier--Stokes, Müller--Israel--Stewart (MIS) and rBRSSS), we investigate the shear response to a periodic drive of varying amplitude $A$ and frequency $\omega$, both analytically in linear response and numerically. We find that, at the linear level, $A\ll 1$, periodically driven systems approach a cyclic attractor that in general differs from Navier--Stokes behaviour. This attractor is universal among kinetic theories and accurately described by MIS theory: for slow driving, $\omega \tau_\pi \ll 1$, where $\tau_\pi$ is the shear relaxation time, it approaches the Navier--Stokes limit, whereas for fast driving the shear stress saturates at its non-interacting (free-streaming) value. In strongly coupled holographic systems, the periodic drive excites non-hydrodynamic quasinormal modes, which produce a characteristic ringing in the approach to the cyclic attractor, in contrast to the purely exponential approach found in kinetic theories. This difference is a direct consequence of the distinct non-hydrodynamic spectra of the two classes of theories. Moreover, unlike in kinetic theory, the holographic response is sensitive to the curvature terms of second-order hydrodynamics. Over longer times, non-linear viscous heating, which is quadratic in the drive amplitude, raises the temperature and thereby lowers $\omega\tau_\pi$, since $\tau_\pi\sim 1/T$. This induces a slow drift of the cyclic attractor, which eventually converges towards Navier--Stokes hydrodynamics at asymptotically late times.

hep-th.title: Two gluon fusion into a $π^0$, $η$, or $η'$ in a relatively weak magnetic field
hep-th.author: Fabio L. Braghin, Enrique Muñoz
hep-th.abstract: In this article, we investigate gluon fusion as a mechanism for neutral meson production ($\pi^0$, $\eta$, and $\eta'$), in the phenomenological context of heavy-ion collisions prior to thermalization, in which a large gluon multiplicity is expected, and when an intense background magnetic field is expected to arise. For this purpose, we computed the ratios of the emission probability rates in the presence of the background magnetic field as compared to vacuum (zero-field), as a function of transverse momenta $p_T$ and energy $\sqrt{s}$, close to midrapidity. Our theoretical results suggest a catalytic effect from the presence of the background magnetic field, that may enhance the neutral pion production by several orders of magnitude at very small energies $s \lesssim 1~\text{GeV}^2$, while the effect is negligible at larger energies $s\gtrsim 10~\text{GeV}^2$. In contrast, the $\eta$ and $\eta'$ production rates are nearly insensitive to the magnetic field presence(as compared to vacuum).

hep-th.title: Smith Algebra from $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Tensor Product Branching via the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko Algebra
hep-th.author: Kohei Hasegawa, Takuya Matsumoto, Akito Takashima
hep-th.abstract: Let $L_n$ be the finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module of highest weight $n$. We study the space of highest-weight vectors in $L_n\otimes L_m$ for the diagonal $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action. The extremal projector constructs these singular vectors and gives operators connecting the highest-weight lines in the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition. We interpret these operators in the Mickelsson-Zhelobenko algebra of the diagonal pair $(\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2, \mathfrak{sl}_2^{\mathrm{diag}})$. A rescaling of their quadratic relation yields the cubic Smith relation $[E,F]=2(H^3-cH)$. This cubic algebra is also known as a Higgs algebra in the physics literature. We express both the central parameter $c$ and the Smith Casimir in terms of the quadratic $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Casimir elements of the two tensor factors. The singular subspace becomes an irreducible Smith module of dimension $\min\{n,m\}+1$, with explicit formulas for the actions of the raising and lowering operators $E$ and $F$. Finally, comparison with finite-dimensional simple Smith modules gives a necessary and sufficient condition for a module to arise from this tensor-product construction.

hep-th.title: Orientations for skein-valued curve counting
hep-th.author: Brett Parker
hep-th.abstract: Ekholm and Shende's skeins-on-branes formalism provides invariant counts of holomorphic curves with boundary on a Maslov zero Lagrangian within a Calabi-Yau 3-fold. This paper proves the orientation relations required for worldsheet skein relations to cancel codimension-one boundary strata. However, standard Cauchy-Riemann Fredholm orientations reveal an unexpected sign puzzle: the orientation relation at a curve with a hyperbolic boundary crossing depends on whether the crossing lies on distinct boundary components or the same component. This domain-dependent sign contradicts the uniform crossing relations of the HOMFLYPT skein algebra. We show that this discrepancy is resolved by passing to an anti-holomorphic orientation convention.We establish all required orientation comparisons in the general setting of an oriented Lagrangian submanifold of a 6-dimensional symplectic manifold.

hep-th.title: Root-of-unity limit of the $A_{n-1}$ lens elliptic gamma function solution of the star-star relation
hep-th.author: Masahito Yamazaki
hep-th.abstract: We study the root-of-unity limit of the multi-component spin solution of the star-star relation whose Boltzmann weights are products of lens elliptic gamma functions, and whose spins take values in $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\times(\mathbb{Z}_r)^{n-1}$. When one of the elliptic nomes tends to a primitive $2rN$-th root of unity, the quasi-classical expansion gives at leading order the classical star-star relation of the Bazhanov-Sergeev multi-spin model; at the next order, under the standard assumptions on the saddle points, a $(\mathbb{Z}_{rN})^{n-1}$-state solution of the star-star relation, which depends on $r$ and $N$ only through $rN$. Real $\mathbb{Z}_n$-symmetric configurations of the continuous spins give elliptic $\mathfrak{sl}(n)$ Kashiwara-Miwa type models labeled by $n$-torsion points. Extended to general primitive torsion points, these include the broken $\mathbb{Z}_{rN}$ model of Quano and Fujii, for which the star-star relation follows from their Yang-Baxter equation when $\gcd(n,rN)=1$. In the trigonometric limit the saddle point equations single out the spectral curve of the $\mathfrak{sl}(n)$ chiral Potts model of Bazhanov, Kashaev, Mangazeev and Stroganov, and the Boltzmann weights become those of that model.

hep-th.title: Quantum Popcorn: the shape of a phase transition bubble
hep-th.author: Kfir Blum, Ipak Fadakar, Omri Rosner, Guilherme L. Pimentel
hep-th.abstract: A quantum tunneling event in field theory is usually depicted as the materialization of a spherical bubble of true vacuum. The bubble appears at rest, and its profile is the time-symmetric slice of Coleman's bounce, the Euclidean solution that controls the decay rate. However, the bubble is spherical only in the leading semiclassical approximation: at the next order the configuration is a Gaussian ensemble of fluctuations around the bounce. We derive the wave functional of the field on the nucleation slice from the half-bounce path integral, and use it to compute the root-mean-square quadrupole moment of a bubble at nucleation. The relative deformation of the bubble wall radius $R$ is $\delta R/R\sim(\hbar/S_b)^{1/2}$, with $S_b$ the bounce action. Thus $\delta R/R\sim0.1$ for a typical cosmological phase transition with $S_b/\hbar\sim100$.

hep-th.title: Phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices in the oscillating axion background
hep-th.author: Naoya Kitajima, Shota Nakagawa
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the effect of an oscillating axion background on thermally induced vortex-antivortex production in the Abelian-Higgs model. Through its coupling to the gauge field, the axion sources an electromagnetic response in the presence of vortex magnetic flux, modifying the dynamics of the vortices. We study this system using Langevin lattice simulations with dissipation and stochastic noise. It is shown that the phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices, namely the pair creation of vortex and antivortex under thermal fluctuations, can be significantly modified in the oscillating axion background. We find that the axion background shifts the rapid increase in the vortex density to lower temperature. In particular, this transition temperature becomes smaller as the oscillation frequency of the axion increases. The temperature dependence of the correlation length is also modified. These features provide a new experimental approach for the axion dark matter using superconducting devices.

hep-th.title: Homogeneous Spectral Freedom and Hadamard Consistency of Perturbative Green Functions
hep-th.author: Bekir Can Lütfüoğlu
hep-th.abstract: Perturbative mode equations often admit formally different particular solutions whose spectral sums appear to have different short-distance singularities. We formulate a general diagnostic which separates this representational freedom from a genuine change of quantum state: for a fixed normally hyperbolic operator, two Hadamard two-point functions can differ only by a smooth homogeneous bisolution. Thus, a nonsmooth term generated by rearranging a perturbative source must be traced either to a changed operator or to inadmissible homogeneous spectral data. We apply the criterion to two impulsive plane-wave backgrounds. Starting directly from the metrics, we recompute the wave operators, modes, world functions, and Van Vleck determinants. Exact-mode matching and the geometrical construction agree through second order for the first profile. In the second, correcting the metric changes the leading perturbation from quadratic to linear order in the wave parameter and eliminates inverse transverse-momentum poles, while the corrected metric retains an exact aligned null-radiation Einstein source. In both examples the singular Green function is precisely the perturbative expansion of the Hadamard parametrix; the additional logarithms arise from momentum-singular homogeneous data. For the exactly soluble first profile, the standard flat-normalized plane-wave prescription gives a vanishing renormalized stress tensor away from the impulsive surface. Smooth-front regularizations of both profiles reproduce, at the calculated orders and away from the characteristic zero mode, the singular structure of the matched impulsive propagators without generating inverse transverse-momentum poles.

hep-th.title: From thermogravity to thermocosmology with a running non-conservation scale
hep-th.author: Emmanuel N. Saridakis
hep-th.abstract: Thermogravity offers a novel approach to cosmic acceleration, deriving trace-free gravitational equations and matter non-conservation from thermodynamic processes in spacetime. We extend this framework towards thermocosmology by introducing a running non-conservation scale $L_2(H)$, while restricting non-conservation to cold dark matter. We investigate two prescriptions, namely a Hubble-proportional rate and an inverse-Hubble running model, deriving their cosmological dynamics and effective geometric dark-energy description. The first admits an exact analytical solution and is related to quadratic running-vacuum cosmologies, while the second approaches standard matter dilution at early times and allows reversals in the direction of energy exchange. Interestingly, the reconstructed geometric dark energy can exhibit quintessence-like and phantom-like behavior, including smooth crossings of the phantom divide, without introducing a phantom field or superacceleration. A unified dynamical-system analysis reveals distinct matter-era critical configurations and a continuous family of de Sitter solutions that are transversely attracting under suitable conditions. Confronting both models with Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae, cosmic chronometers, and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, we find a mild preference for positive present-day matter non-conservation. The Akaike information criterion slightly favors the thermogravity scenarios, whereas the Bayesian information criterion favors the simpler $\Lambda$CDM model. Thus, running thermocosmology provides a viable framework for nontrivial effective dark-energy dynamics.

hep-th.title: Two-loop matter power spectrum from FFTLog and kite integrals
hep-th.author: Paola Cappellazzi, Johannes M. Henn, Marko Simonović
hep-th.abstract: We present a fast and accurate method for computing the two-loop matter power spectrum in the Effective Field Theory of Large-Scale Structure (EFTofLSS). Using FFTLog, we decompose the linear power spectrum into complex power laws, reducing the two-loop corrections to cosmology-independent massless Feynman integrals of kite topology. A central numerical challenge is the evaluation of these integrals for complex powers with large imaginary parts, where the highly oscillatory integrands make accurate numerical evaluation particularly challenging. We overcome this difficulty using a Mellin--Barnes representation summed over a uniform lattice, achieving approximately ten digit precision even for large imaginary powers, with an error estimate for each integral. The resulting precomputed matrices allow the two-loop power spectrum to be evaluated for a new cosmology in a few milliseconds. Comparing with direct numerical integration, we find agreement at the $10^{-4}$ level relative to the power spectrum up to $k=0.2$ $h$Mpc$^{-1}$ after accounting for EFTofLSS counterterm contributions and FFTLog decomposition errors. The same framework extends to biased tracers and redshift-space distortions, providing the building blocks for general two-loop calculations in EFTofLSS. We make the code for evaluating the kite integrals publicly available, together with precomputed matrices and an implementation for the two-loop matter power spectrum as a concrete application. Our results can be directly incorporated into existing FFTLog-based codes for large-scale structure, extending their current one-loop capabilities to two loops within the same computational framework.

hep-th.title: Anomalies of TQFTs coupled to parameter spaces and constraints on ground-state degeneracies
hep-th.author: Takamasa Ando, Ryan Thorngren
hep-th.abstract: Anomalies of global symmetries can arise in long-range entangled quantum many-body systems and provide useful constraints on their dynamics. In this paper, we study anomalies of $d$-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs) coupled to parameter spaces and their implications for ground-state degeneracies. Specifically, we formulate anomalies as obstructions to constructing parametrized families of TQFTs. We discuss how the classification of these anomalies depends on the choice of topology on the universal $\mathrm{U}(1)$ $(d-1)$-form symmetry. In this framework, we use the projective ground-state bundle obtained by compactifying the TQFT on a spatial manifold to derive a general constraint relating its ground-state degeneracy $N$ to its torsion anomaly $\omega$, expressed as $N\int_W\omega\in\mathbb{Z}$ for bundles $W$ of spatial manifolds over closed surfaces. We apply this constraint to ground-state degeneracies of (2+1)-dimensional TQFTs with framing and 1-form symmetry anomalies and to obstructions to symmetry-preserving TQFTs. We also discuss implications for bordism generators and propose a conjecture on anomaly detection by manifolds fibered over surfaces.

hep-th.title: Baker--Akhiezer sections from Higgs bundles and Landau levels in hyperbolic band theory
hep-th.author: Duong Dinh, Steven Rayan
hep-th.abstract: As observed by Kienzle and the second author, rank-two $\mathcal{O}(3)$-twisted Higgs bundles on the projective line encode all hyperbolic crystals of genus two: the spectral curves are the unit cells, and the Hitchin fibers are the abelian Brillouin zones. In a uniform magnetic field of two flux quanta, the lowest Landau level is one-dimensional at every nonzero momentum, and, as found by Iengo and Li, its dimension jumps to two at the zero momentum. We identify the states of the lowest Landau level with the Baker--Akhiezer sections of the Higgs bundles, and their zeros, the vortices, with the Baker--Akhiezer divisors. A family of nonzero momenta limits to the zero momentum exactly when each of the two vortices approaches the image of the other under the spatial inversion, and the states of the jumped level are labeled by the directions of limiting. On the Higgs bundle side, the zero momentum is the point where the Hitchin fiber intersects the Hitchin section. Such a family of Higgs bundles limits to the Hitchin section, thereby crossing to a lower stratum of the \BB stratification, an example of the phenomenon investigated in terms of Baker--Akhiezer divisors by the first author with Figiel and Teschner.

hep-th.title: A mini-course on Generalized Symmetries and a relation to Cobordisms and K-theory
hep-th.author: Oscar Loaiza-Brito, Víctor M. López-Ramos
hep-th.abstract: This mini-course, conducted at the XI School on Geometric, Algebraic, and Topological Methods in Quantum Field Theory held in Villa de Leyva, Colombia, provides an overview of the interconnection between generalized symmetries and cohomology. It is designed for advanced undergraduate students with a background in physics or mathematics. Additionally, we describe a method for connecting generalized symmetries with cobordisms and K-theory within the framework of string theory. We assume basic knowledge in quantum field theory and differential forms.

hep-th.title: Gravitational dressing: from the crossed product to more general algebraic and mathematical structure
hep-th.author: Steven B. Giddings
hep-th.abstract: The crossed product, and consequent transition from von Neumann algebras of type III to II, is recovered from a truncation of more general gravitational dressing constructions, about certain spacetimes. This is done by extending "standard dressing" constructions previously used to give a perturbative definition of "gravitational splittings," defining approximate localization of information. This result appears to illustrate that this algebraic transition is a small piece of a more general algebraic, or other mathematical, structure associated with quantum gravity. The leading-order structure involves noncommutativity from separated regions, and at the nonperturbative level connects with a possible explanation of holographic behavior for gravity.

hep-th.title: Black hole thermodynamics at null infinity. Part 1: Dual Generalized Second Law
hep-th.author: Antoine Rignon-Bret, Matthieu Vilatte
hep-th.abstract: The generalized second law (GSL) of black hole thermodynamics asserts the monotonic increase of the generalized entropy combining the black hole area and the entropy of quantum fields outside the horizon. Modern proofs of the GSL rely on information theoretic methods and are typically formulated using algebras of observables defined on the event horizon together with a vacuum state invariant under horizon symmetries, inducing a geometric modular flow. In this work, we formulate a dual version of the generalized second law from the perspective of asymptotic observers at future null infinity, who do not have access to the black hole area. Our approach exploits the dependence of the second law on the choice of algebra of observables and of a reference state invariant under suitable symmetries, in close analogy with open quantum thermodynamics. Using algebraic quantum field theory and modular theory, we analyze several physically motivated vacuum states, including the Hartle Hawking state and two classes of regularized vacua. We show that, at null infinity, the monotonic quantity governing an irreversible evolution is no longer the generalized entropy, but rather a thermodynamic potential constructed from asymptotic observables. Depending on the chosen vacuum, this potential takes the form of the free energy or of a generalized grand potential built from the Bondi mass and additional (angular) mode dependent chemical potentials. The resulting inequalities define a dual generalized second law at future null infinity, which can be consistently combined with the standard GSL involving variations of the black hole area.

hep-th.title: Black hole thermodynamics at null infinity. Part 2: Open systems, Markovian dynamics and work extraction from non-rotating black holes
hep-th.author: Antoine Rignon-Bret, Matthieu Vilatte
hep-th.abstract: Black hole thermodynamics provides a unique setting in which general relativity, quantum field theory, and statistical mechanics converge. In semiclassical gravity, this interplay culminates in the generalized second law (GSL), whose modern proofs rely on information theoretic techniques applied to algebras of observables defined on null hypersurfaces. These proofs exhibit close structural parallels with the thermodynamics of open quantum systems governed by Markovian dynamics. In this work, we draw parallels between the dynamics of quantum fields in regions bounded by non expanding causal horizons and the thermodynamics of quantum systems weakly coupled to equilibrium reservoirs. We introduce a dictionary relating late time boundary conditions to the choice of reservoir, vacuum states to fixed points of the dynamics, and modular Hamiltonians to thermodynamic potentials. Building on results from a companion paper on dual generalized second laws at future null infinity, we show that additional terms appearing in the associated thermodynamic potentials admit a natural interpretation as work contributions. We demonstrate that certain non thermal vacuum states at null infinity allow for the operation of autonomous thermal engines and enable work extraction from the radiation. Extending the analysis to the Unruh vacuum in Schwarzschild and Kerr backgrounds, we obtain generalized grand potential type laws incorporating grey body effects and angular momentum fluxes. Altogether, our results clarify the thermodynamic description of black hole dynamics and place it within the broader framework of open quantum thermodynamics.

hep-th.title: On the Cosmological Constant in Pre-geometric Gravity
hep-th.author: Andrea Addazi, Giuseppe Meluccio
hep-th.abstract: We offer novel perspectives on the cosmological constant (CC) problem, aiming toward a potential solution that requires neither fine-tuning nor anthropic arguments. In pre-geometric gravity (PGG), spacetime emerges from the spontaneous breaking of a fundamental gauge symmetry. This mechanism dynamically generates general relativity while also revealing a deep connection: the topological Gauss-Bonnet coupling of the theory scales precisely as the de Sitter entropy, an enormous number which reflects the information content of our universe. This coupling acts as a gravitational $\theta$-angle parameter, forcing the CC to become quantized into discrete topological sectors. The symmetry-breaking dynamics naturally selects the sector corresponding to the observed vacuum energy. The selected vacuum state is stabilized by the extremely large potential barrier of the pre-geometric Higgs field, which effectively seals it off from quantum tunneling transitions to other topological sectors. The PGG framework could thus provide a dynamical explanation for the smallness of the CC, linking gravity, topology and quantum information in a unified picture.

hep-th.title: Lattice Realizations of Flat Gauging and T-duality Defects at Any Radius
hep-th.author: Riccardo Argurio, Giovanni Galati, Nathan Godechal
hep-th.abstract: We analyze non-invertible topological interfaces and defects in the two-dimensional compact boson, focusing on the more exotic ones obtained by gauging continuous symmetries with flat connections on a half-space. These include interfaces between mutually irrational radii and T-duality symmetries at arbitrary boson radius. Using the modified Villain discretization on both a Euclidean two-dimensional square lattice and a quantum one-dimensional chain, we show that all these topological interfaces survive discretization and give rise to non-compact edge modes localized at the defect sites. Such non-compact edge modes imply a continuous defect spectrum and an infinite quantum dimension. In the special case of rational radii, we show how the defect action or Hamiltonian can be modified in order to compactify the edge modes and produce more standard defects with finite quantum dimension.

hep-th.title: $T\overline{T}$ correlators from tensionless strings
hep-th.author: Andrea Dei, Kiarash Naderi
hep-th.abstract: Motivated by earlier approaches, we develop a worldsheet framework for computing correlation functions in the single trace $T \overline{T}$-deformed tensionless AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ duality. By describing the deformed bulk theory as a Berkovits-Vafa $\mathcal{N}=4$ topological string, we obtain a consistent definition of physical states and correlation functions, yielding a tractable setup for testing aspects of holography beyond AdS/CFT. We construct deformed physical vertex operators and compute their tree-level two-point functions exactly. We discuss the relation of our results to previous proposals for $T \overline{T}$-deformed two-point functions obtained from alternative worldsheet approaches, JT gravity, and perturbative field theory computations.

hep-th.title: Algorithmic Dualization of Unitary Circular Quivers
hep-th.author: Riccardo Comi, Chiung Hwang, Fabio Marino
hep-th.abstract: We introduce a field-theoretic algorithm to find the $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ duality web of 3d $\mathcal{N}=4$ circular quiver theories with unitary gauge groups, extending the algorithm for linear quivers. Although circular and linear quivers share the same local structure, the circular topology requires additional ingredients, which we formulate in terms of topological and baryonic QFT blocks, together with new $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ duality moves acting on them. For good circular quivers, this provides a field-theoretic derivation of mirror symmetry and extends it to the full $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ duality web. We then study bad circular quivers, distinguishing between local badness, associated with under-balanced gauge nodes, and global badness, arising from the circular topology itself. In particular, we analyze the magnetic and electric dual frames of globally bad circular quivers and provide additional evidence for the proposed duality by matching the Higgs branch index with the dual Coulomb branch index. The latter exhibits a structure reminiscent of permutation-group gauging and reveals a refined relation to the ADHM quiver, flowing to the $\mathcal{N}=8$ infrared fixed point.

hep-th.title: World-Line Actions in Weyl Geometry
hep-th.author: Cezar Condeescu, Andrei Micu
hep-th.abstract: In this note we construct, from a gauge theory perspective, the world-line action for a particle moving on a time-like curve in Weyl geometry. The action we find is dimensionless, Weyl invariant, additive and, in general, non-local due to an open Wilson line which we have to add in order to account for a general Weyl field. In special cases, this Wilson line can be local, but the geometry becomes integrable. The action can not be used to measure the proper time as it is dimensionless and no mass parameter is allowed in the symmetric phase of the theory. We show that the usual conditions for defining proper time: affine parametrization, dimension of time and additivity supplemented by the requirement of Weyl invariance can not be fulfilled simultaneously and therefore no satisfactory notion of proper time exists in the symmetric phase. Under spontaneous symmetry breaking the particle acquires a mass, the action becomes Riemannian and the proper time can be again defined. We also construct a classically equivalent quadratic action by using an einbein on the world-line and show that the non-locality can be seen to arise from integrating out a constrained field.

hep-th.title: Wavefunctions of AdS$_3$ Universes and $T\bar{T}$-deformed Torus Partition Functions
hep-th.author: Shinji Hirano
hep-th.abstract: We study wavefunctions of quantum gravity in asymptotically AdS$_3$ spacetimes and their relation to $T\bar{T}$-deformed torus partition functions. We show that the deformed partition function is given by an invertible integral transform of bulk wavefunctions, which implements a change of representation from the York time to its conjugate, the spatial volume. The invertibility of the transform allows the bulk wavefunction to be reconstructed from the family of $T\bar{T}$-deformed partition functions. A $T\bar{T}$-deformed partition function at fixed coupling is the amplitude of the bulk state in a finite-width, fixed-volume wavepacket localized at the asymptotic boundary in York time. In the CFT limit, the wavepacket localizes at the boundary, recovering the standard holographic relation. The holographic screen of a given state is the support of the integrand of the transform: at large central charge, it separates from the wavepacket and reproduces finite-cutoff holography for the sign of the coupling with complex energies, and glue-on holography for the opposite sign. In Euclidean signature, the construction arises naturally from wavefunctions of Rindler AdS$_3$, while after a double Wick rotation it admits a Lorentzian interpretation in terms of closed AdS$_3$ torus universes without asymptotic boundaries. We also discuss de Sitter torus universes and generalizations to other spatial topologies and higher dimensions.

hep-th.title: Monodromy defects in ABJM theory and integrability
hep-th.author: Charlotte Kristjansen, Andrey Shusharin
hep-th.abstract: We establish that supersymmetric monodromy defects in ABJM theory, also known as vortex loops, define integrable boundary states of the underlying alternating SU(4) spin chain. Exploiting the KT relation within the framework of the algebraic Bethe ansatz, we derive a closed-form expression for the leading-order one-point functions of non- protected operators in the presence of these defects. As a special case, our result reproduces the spin-chain overlap governing the three-point functions of two maximal giant gravitons and a single tiny graviton. We furthermore investigate the quantization of the theory in the defect background and compute the first quantum correction to the one-point functions in the simplest setting. Finally, we discuss possible extensions of our overlap formula.

hep-th.title: An Infinite Family of Non-Rational VOAs from Strongly Coupled 4d Higgsless SCFTs
hep-th.author: Hongliang Jiang
hep-th.abstract: We study an infinite family of strongly coupled four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ superconformal field theories (SCFTs) distinguished by a trivial Higgs branch, known as the $(A_2,D_{3m+1})$ Argyre-Douglas theories. We propose that their associated vertex operator algebras (VOAs) are the doublet algebras $\mathcal A(4m+2)$, an infinite family of non-rational vertex operator superalgebras with a remarkably simple strong generating set of only three fields. We provide several highly nontrivial checks of this proposal. In particular, we reproduce the four-dimensional conformal anomalies $a$ and $c$ from the VOA and analytically prove the exact equality between the Schur index of the SCFT and the supercharacter of the VOA. A key ingredient is a diagonal-gauging realization of the $(A_2,D_{3m+1})$ theories in terms of two simpler building blocks, which makes the Schur-index computation tractable. Remarkably, we find that the resulting Schur index of the $(A_2,D_{3m+1})$ theory coincides with that of $\mathcal N=4$ $SU(2)$ Super-Yang-Mills theory, up to an overall prefactor and an appropriate identification of fugacities. We also discuss a generalization to the two-parameter family $(A_{2s},D_{(2s+1)m+1})$, whose members likewise have trivial Higgs branches and admit diagonal-gauging realizations. A particularly interesting subfamily is $(A_{2s},D_{2s+2})$, for which the four-dimensional conformal anomalies coincide, $a=c$. As a byproduct, we also show that the doublet VOA $\mathcal A(4m+2)$ is not classically free for positive integer $m $, and we discuss its implications for the Schur and Macdonald indices. Our results reveal a systematic connection between Higgsless SCFTs, diagonal gauging, and strongly finite but non-rational vertex operator algebras.

hep-th.title: Informational and algebraic renormalization group
hep-th.author: Takato Mori, Teruaki Nagasawa
hep-th.abstract: Renormalization group (RG) is a core concept from statistical mechanics to quantum field theory, yet its schemes differ widely across literature. We formulate Wilsonian RG for generic, including finite-dimensional, quantum systems as a quantum channel combining coarse graining with isometric rescaling, whose Kraus representation yields pure conditional trajectories for pure inputs and recovers mixed-state flows upon averaging. We then develop an algebraic extension without assuming tensor-product factorization: the retained low-energy algebra is constructed from the one-particle spectrum, and coarse graining is a conditional expectation onto it. Identifying the channel's Cesàro mean with a resource-destroying map onto fixed states establishes a resource theory of RG and yields a relative-entropy monotone without variational optimization. For thermal states in the zero-temperature limit, the resulting Bogoliubov--Kubo--Mori metric per unit spacetime volume is proportional to the Zamolodchikov metric, directly relating the resource density to $c-c_{\rm IR}$ near a two-dimensional IR fixed point. We also introduce the relative entropy of coarse graining to measure discarded UV information, prove its monotonicity along successive coarse grainings, and evaluate it holographically in global $\mathrm{AdS}_3$.

hep-th.title: The Phenomenology of the Dark Dimension and Non-Supersymmetric Strings
hep-th.author: Cumrun Vafa
hep-th.abstract: Swampland principles, combined with the smallness of dark energy $\Lambda$, lead to the dark dimension scenario, with one extra dimension of micron size. We review this scenario and its predictions: KK graviton dark matter (or the KK tower of the quintessence field into which the gravitons convert), neutrino masses tied to $\Lambda^{1/4}$ via a bulk $B-L$ gauge symmetry, QCD axion decay constant $f_a\sim \Lambda^{1/12}\sim 10^9-10^{10}$ GeV at the 5d Planck scale $M_5$, connecting electroweak hierarchy to $\Lambda^{1/6}$, and a relation between the GUT and weak scales with $M_5$ as the geometric mean. The dark dimension also provides a concrete realization of an evolving dark sector: the evolution of its diameter correlates the variation of dark energy with that of the dark matter mass, fitting the recent DESI DR2 (+CMB+supernovae) data while avoiding the phantom crossing that the $w_0w_a$CDM parametrization would suggest---the apparent phantom behavior instead arises from the evolving dark matter mass. The fits suggest that the dark energy field sits in the interior of moduli space, near an unstable critical point. Motivated by this, we review recent progress on non-supersymmetric string vacua: isolated critical points protected by duality symmetries, in non-geometric flux compactifications and in Scherk--Schwarz compactifications of M-theory, and an emerging duality web for non-supersymmetric strings. This note is based on two talks given by the author at String Phenomenology 2026 (Paris) and Strings 2026 (Shanghai).

hep-th.title: New topological phase transitions in $κ$-deformed $ϕ^4$ lattice models
hep-th.author: Adith A, A. Bhagwat
hep-th.abstract: This paper explores topological phase transitions in the momentum space of the $\kappa$-deformed $\phi^4$ lattice model within the mean-field approximation. We show that the double-well structure of the momentum space gives rise to degenerate momentum states at high energies and that this change is marked by a phase transition. We investigate this transition using both numerical and analytical methods, with the analytical approach based primarily on singularity theory. Our numerical analysis shows that the energy at which the topological phase transition occurs is related to the noncommutative parameter by the simple power law $E \sim 1/\alpha^{4}$. By mapping the constant-energy-level surface to the $A_{3}$ singularity, we obtain the same result analytically. We also present results unique to noncommutative systems, showing that the fraction of particles in degenerate momentum states has a nonzero commutative limit. As a nonperturbative effect, this result provides a testable prediction for the existence of noncommutative spacetime.

hep-th.title: Black hole cohomologies in N=4 SYM
hep-th.author: Seunggyu Kim, Jehyun Lee, Siyul Lee, Jaewon Song
hep-th.abstract: We systematically investigate BPS cohomologies of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory with gauge group SU$(N)$ with $N=2, 3, 4$, focusing primarily on the BMN sector. We find non-Coulomb graviton cohomologies for $N>2$. For $N>2$, the lightest black hole cohomology in the BMN sector always carries non-trivial $R$-charge and corresponds to the brane-fused type. Therefore, the `core' black holes without hair are `heavier'. We also find that a family of brane-fused cohomologies in $N=3$ is not lifted at the first quantum order. At a fixed charge sector, gravitons carry definite parity under charge conjugation. Up to the levels we have tested, every black hole cohomology either has opposite parity to that of gravitons or is lifted by quantum corrections. We conjecture that black hole cohomologies always carry parity opposite to gravitons in the same charge sector.

hep-th.title: Boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in holography
hep-th.author: Yu Shi, Xinwu Liu, Liping Li, Chikun Ding, Yuebing Zhou, Changqing Liu, Sheng Long
hep-th.abstract: We study the boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in a probe Abelian Higgs model on a fixed AdS black brane. Different drives ending at the same charge density can prepare states with different slow mode amplitudes and relaxation behavior. Two pulses cancel the slowest mode at linear order, but charge exchange during preparation and radial Maxwell feedback regenerate the slow tail at cubic order. We derive the complete cubic correction from the lower order field equations, including feedback after source removal, and use it to predict a compensating pulse. Full nonlinear evolution confirms that cubic compensation reduces the residual slow amplitude from $O(\epsilon^3)$ to $O(\epsilon^5)$. For a representative protocol at final density $\rho_f=3$ and $\epsilon=0.05$, cubic compensation suppresses the slow amplitude by a factor of about $600$ relative to the linear prescription. Cubic compensation extends the period of fast relaxation without changing the final quasinormal mode spectrum. Further nonlinear tuning suppresses the residual slow amplitude to the level of numerical resolution. The excess free energy of the prepared states can exceed that of a weakly driven reference at release and fall below it during subsequent relaxation. Three pulses also suppress a second slow channel over the resolved time window and reveal interference between faster modes. Starting from a common initial state, controls with zero net charge transfer reach a given relaxation threshold sooner than passive relaxation, even when the full control duration is included.

hep-th.title: Large-Level Limit of Doubled Chern-Simons Theory Part I: Regular Sector, Boundaries and Interfaces
hep-th.author: Shengyi Guan, Qiang Jia, Jiahua Tian, Yi-Nan Wang
hep-th.abstract: We study three-dimensional $BF$ theory as the large-level limit of the doubled Chern-Simons theory $G_k\times G_{-k}$ for simply connected, compact, simple $G$, a limit that connects the symmetry topological field theories of finite and continuous symmetries. Lines whose two highest weights grow linearly with $k$ at fixed difference become $BF$ lines, with magnetic flux set by their average and electric charge equal to their difference. Representing level-$k$ torus states as normalized flux-charge wave packets, we prove that every fixed modular transformation of any fixed normalizable state with regular flux converges in the strong-$*$ topology to its $BF$ counterpart. The Dehn twist gives each line exactly its Aharonov-Bohm phase at every level, while $S$ converges to a Fourier transform exchanging flux and charge, without escaping to singular holonomies or large charges. States that approach singular fluxes at large $k$ are not covered. The natural boundary 2d theory is speculated to be a decompactified boson in the abelian case $G=U(1)$, and $\dim G$ non-compact free scalars for general $G$. For $SU(2)$, we discuss the gapped interfaces between adjacent levels, which must shift some flux or charge by a finite amount. In the $k\rightarrow\infty$ limit the interface is conjectured to be the $c=1$ Runkel-Watts theory.

hep-th.title: Unitarity Methods for Magnus Amplitudes
hep-th.author: Jung-Wook Kim, Sungsoo Kim, Jian-Rong Li
hep-th.abstract: Magnus amplitudes refer to the matrix elements of the logarithm of the $S$-matrix. Modern unitarity methods construct cut-constructible parts of scattering amplitudes without directly invoking Feynman diagrams, offering an efficient way of obtaining loop integrands for scattering amplitudes. A procedure is proposed that adapts unitarity methods to the computation of Magnus amplitudes by modifying the $i0^+$ prescriptions of scattering amplitude integrands. A sufficient condition for applying the procedure at the level of master integrals is identified.

hep-th.title: Kasner Exponents from the Bouncing Singularity
hep-th.author: Hyunwoo Oh
hep-th.abstract: Thermal two-point functions of holographic CFTs can probe the black hole singularity. When a bouncing geodesic exists, the correlator at leading order in $1/N$ develops a singularity $G(t, \vec{x}=0) \propto (t_c-t)^{-2\Delta+b_t}$, where $\Delta$ is the scaling dimension of the operator. We show that the additional exponent $b_t$ is determined by the Kasner exponents near the singularity. From the wave reflected off the singularity, which gives an exponentially small term in the large-frequency retarded correlator, we derive the formula $b_t=(d-1) \max \left( \frac{p_i-p_t}{1-p_t}, \frac{1}{2} \right)$ for planar black branes in AdS$_{d+1}$, where $p_t$ and $p_i$ are the Kasner exponents of the time and spatial directions. We compare our formula with the numerical values of Čeplak and Valach. It reproduces the relation that they proposed for a special class of black branes. For more general black branes, where no formula had been found, our formula agrees with most of their numerical data and fits them much better than the extension of their relation. We also give predictions for $b_t$ in theories where the Kasner exponents are known, but $b_t$ has not been computed.

hep-th.title: Revisiting monodromy defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories
hep-th.author: Jiechao Feng, Nayan Myerson-Jain, G. Shankar, Taige Wang, Meng Cheng
hep-th.abstract: Monodromy defects are fundamental objects in extended quantum systems with global symmetries. We study such defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories (CFT), which describe the universality class of $\text{O}(N)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking transitions. In particular, we consider partial-monodromy defects, whose corresponding symmetry transformations only act on a subset of the fundamental $\text{O}(N)$ vector field. We develop an analytical theory of the defect phases, using both renormalization group and large $N$ expansion. In general (spacetime) dimensions $3\leq d<4$, multiple defect CFTs are identified, which are described by appropriate boundary conditions for the vector field near the defect. Near $d=3$, we show that in the large $N$ limit, a stable defect CFT always exists, characterized by the so-called ("standard") "alternate" boundary conditions for the (twisted) untwisted fields, whose defect correlations are (suppressed) enhanced. We then perform large-scale classical Monte Carlo simulations of monodromy defects in the O(3) CFT in an improved lattice model and numerically extract the defect scaling dimensions. The numerical results are in qualitative agreement with the stable defect CFT identified in the field theory.

hep-th.title: The Topological String on the Quintic to Genus 83 and the Rank-Two D4-D2-D0 Indices
hep-th.author: Michael Hecht
hep-th.abstract: We compute quintic Gopakumar-Vafa invariants for genera 2-83 and degrees up to 44 by integrating the holomorphic anomaly equations. Under rank-one modularity for the required Gieseker invariants and rank-two charge conjugation, a coupled system of boundary and surplus wall-crossing equations fixes the holomorphic ambiguities and 22 of the 36 polar rank-two D4-D2-D0 coefficients, without assuming any rank-two index. A computer-assisted extension of wall crossing supplies additional equations and the boundary datum needed to close the recursion through genus 83. With known low-genus input, the GV data are complete through degree 32 and yield PT and DT tables. Selected higher-genus wall-crossing invariants reach genus 216; 33 entries require additional hypotheses. Retrospectively selected extrapolations give conditional candidates at genera 84 and 85 and, with rank-two mock modularity, for the remaining polar coefficients.

hep-th.title: Quantum Riemannian Hamiltonian Descent
hep-th.author: Yoshihiko Abe, Ryo Nagai
hep-th.abstract: We propose Quantum Riemannian Hamiltonian Descent (QRHD), a quantum algorithm for continuous optimization on Riemannian manifolds that extends Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD) by incorporating geometric structure of the parameter space via a position-dependent metric in the kinetic term. We formulate QRHD in both operator and path integral formalisms and derive the corresponding quantum equations of motion, showing that quantum corrections appear in the action integral but they are suppressed at late times by the time-dependent dissipation factor. This implies that convergence near optimal points is controlled by the classical potential while quantum effects influence early-time dynamics. By analyzing the semiclassical equation, we estimate a lower bound on the convergence time and numerically demonstrate whether QRHD works as a quantum optimization algorithm in some examples. A quantum circuit implementation based on time-dependent Hamiltonian simulation is also discussed and the query complexity is estimated.

hep-th.title: Black Hole Dynamics at Fifth Post-Newtonian Order
hep-th.author: Rafael A. Porto, Massimiliano M. Riva
hep-th.abstract:
Using the worldline action in [2409.05860], we derive the total even-in-velocity (relative) impulse, scattering angle, and time delay at fifth post-Newtonian (5PN) order, including radiation-reaction and hereditary contributions at ${\cal O}(G^5
u^2)$ and ${\cal O}(G^6
u^2)$. We introduce an isotropic-like description which, together with the associated losses of energy and angular momentum, fixes the evolution of the system from scattering data. This framework opens the door to an unambiguous characterization of the underlying two-body dynamics solely in terms of scattering observables. Following [2409.05860], we isolate a conservative component using Feynman's $i0^+$ prescription. This sector contains both "tail-like" and "memory-like" contributions, the latter being nonlocal in time and described by a double Principal-Value integral. Owing to the local-in-time character of the corresponding (in-in) action, we establish a systematic procedure that is consistent with Feynman's prescription while preserving the complete local dynamics. This provides a universal contribution to the conservative (isotropic) Hamiltonian at 5PN order and, as a byproduct, also fixes the value of the Effective One Body coefficients $\{{ ar d}_{5{m loc}}, a_{6{m loc}}\}$ consistently with the Tutti-Frutti framework. For completeness, we analyse the "$\gamma	ext{-}3$" prescription introduced in recent post-Minkowskian computations. When implemented in our formalism, we find exact agreement over the overlapping regime of validity. In contrast, Feynman's prescription yields a (local) memory-like contribution with the opposite sign at ${\cal O}(G^5
u^2)$. We also find that an analogous $\gamma	ext{-}3$ rerouting at ${\cal O}(G^6
u^2)$ would be incompatible with the conjecture that all $\pi^2$ terms arise solely from the potential region, while Feynman's formulation preserves this expectation.

hep-th.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Building Analytic Quantum Circuits: the Case of Diagonal Operators
hep-th.author: Matvei Fedin, Andrey Morozov
hep-th.abstract: Machine Learning has become a useful instrument across many fields, but the opacity of typical ``black-box'' models limits their value for scientific discovery. In this paper we present a methodology that uses \emph{interpretable} Machine Learning to generate analytic mathematical hypotheses about a physical system, which can then be confirmed by a formal derivation. We demonstrate the methodology on the problem of decomposing unitary operators into elementary quantum gates. By training an interpretable model on circuits obtained numerically and analyzing its weights, we are led to a hypothesis for the analytic structure of the decomposition. Applied to the family of diagonal operators, this hypothesis yields a universal, analytic quantum circuit valid for an arbitrary number of qubits, whose $CNOT$ count scales as $\mathcal{O}(2^n)$, improving on the $\mathcal{O}(2.5^n)$ of standard numerical methods. The resulting decomposition is proved rigorously in a companion paper.

hep-th.title: Vector modes in Type 3 New GR
hep-th.author: Alexey Golovnev
hep-th.abstract: Some time ago, we published the full count of degrees of freedom in the linearised weak gravity limit of arbitrary New GR models. We did it by considering the linear weak gravity equations and presented a thorough analysis with no ambiguity left. A bit later, we generalised it to linear cosmological perturbations and discussed the strong coupling issues that appear already at this level. Recently, there were claims that some dynamical modes had been missed in our work. However, the authors of the new claims did not look at the equations of motion and analysed the quadratic Lagrangian densities instead. In this paper, I take one of the most elementary cases, namely the vector modes in New GR of Type 3, and show what was their mistake that had led them to claiming that those were dynamical. The main message: Do not substitute constraint equations into a Lagrangian.

hep-th.title: The Status of Single Scalar Field Dark Energy
hep-th.author: Carlos García-García, Pedro G. Ferreira, William J. Wolf
hep-th.abstract: We present an assessment of the current observational status of single scalar field models of dark energy. Motivated by recent cosmological measurements -- including baryon acoustic oscillations, Type Ia supernovae, and CMB data -- we examine whether a dynamical scalar field offers a viable explanation for the accelerated expansion of the Universe. Working within an effective field theory (EFT) framework, we argue that cosmological observations are fundamentally limited and can at most constrain a small number of parameters that govern scalar field dynamics. We show that quintessence remains only marginally distinguishable from a cosmological constant, $\Lambda$, and that more general EFT extensions exhibit modest statistical preference, though such evidence is sensitive to data set selection and prior assumptions. These extended models generically predict fifth forces and modifications to the growth of structure, raising challenges from astrophysical constraints. We compare their predictions with current growth rate measurements, Integrated Sachs-Wolfe (ISW) effect and Solar System constraints. We emphasize that viable screening mechanisms remain theoretically non-trivial and observationally testable. On the other hand, we find that current ISW and growth data remain largely in agreement. Looking ahead to Stage IV surveys we forecast improvements in constraints on the dark energy behaviour; although there will be some tightening of bounds, we argue that the problem of underdetermination will persist. We conclude that while single scalar field dark energy remains a natural and flexible framework, its ultimate viability will hinge on improved low-redshift growth measurements and a clearer understanding of gravitational screening.

hep-th.title: Non-Clifford quantum cellular automata from invertible topological quantum field theories
hep-th.author: Meng Sun, Zongyuan Wang, Bowen Yang, Nathanan Tantivasadakarn, Yu-An Chen
hep-th.abstract: Quantum cellular automata (QCAs) describe locality-preserving quantum dynamics and link quantum information, many-body physics, and topological quantum field theory (TQFT). Constructing a QCA from a TQFT, however, remains challenging: although a topological action yields a Hamiltonian with commuting terms that realizes the desired ground state, it does not by itself specify an automorphism of the full operator algebra. We develop a unified algebraic construction that extends such Hamiltonians to complete separator-flipper algebras on the full tensor-product Hilbert space, thereby defining the corresponding QCAs microscopically. In 3 spatial dimensions, our framework unifies all previously known QCA constructions associated with the $\mathbb{Z}_8\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ subgroup of the Witt group, including the $U(1)_2$ and $U(1)_4$ QCAs. The same algebraic structure yields new infinite families of generalized $U(1)_2$ and $U(1)_4$ non-Clifford QCAs in spatial dimensions $d=4k-1$. We also reformulate the 4-dimensional $w_2w_3$ QCA and use it to construct QCAs from TQFTs associated with arbitrary products of Stiefel--Whitney classes. For example, we explicitly construct two infinite families: $w_2^nw_3^m$ QCAs in dimension $d=2n+3m-1$ and $w_2w_{4k-1}$ QCAs in dimension $d=4k$. For the 5-dimensional $w_3^2$ and $w_2^3$ QCAs, our construction gives finite-depth quantum circuits, consistent with the cobordism classification. More generally, we show that our construction yields a finite-depth quantum circuit whenever the corresponding Stiefel-Whitney number vanishes on every closed oriented manifold. Overall, these results convert invertible TQFTs into microscopic QCAs, provide higher-dimensional constructions beyond the Clifford setting, and open a systematic route to characterizing their stable structures and boundary anomalies.

hep-th.title: Application of flavor moonshine
hep-th.author: Hirotaka Sugawara
hep-th.abstract: In our previous paper [1], we presented the application of Moonshine to the flavor physics based on the work of Cohn and Deutsch and Bagger and Wess [2], J. Conway and S. Norton [3] andthis http URL,this http URLandthis http URL[4] laid down the mathematical basics. We present here the extension of our previous paper [1] by including the supersymmetry in addition to the modular symmetry [1], [4]. We calculate all the lepton masses and the quark masses and their super partner masses by using the one input particle mass for each family. The two valued modular function is defined in equation (3.7). We define the two valued modular function of degree K in equation (3.2). We use K = 1 two valued modular function for the charged leptons and K = 2 two valued modular function for the neutrino and for the up quarks, and K = 3 two valued modular function for the down quarks, where 2K is the level of the two valued modular function. We emphasize that we have three particle masses which can be measured by the existing accelerators such as KEK B factory or CERN LHC. One is super electron mass "M_{e,s} = 24.73MeV", which is approximately 25 times that of electron. The Super d, s and b quark masses are 0GeV, 89.165GeV, and 2964.7GeV. Super down quark mass is 0 and super strange quark mass can be measured both in KEKB and in CERN LHC. The super bottom quark mass can be measured only in LHC.

hep-th.title: Early- and late-time constraints on Wald-Gauss-Bonnet topological dark energy and implications for the $H_0$ and $S_8$ tensions
hep-th.author: Stylianos A. Tsilioukas, Fotios K. Anagnostopoulos, Spyros Basilakos, Andronikos Paliathanasis, Emmanuel N. Saridakis
hep-th.abstract: The persistent $H_0$ and $S_8$ tensions motivate the search for new dark-energy mechanisms capable of modifying the late-time expansion history while preserving the successful early-Universe predictions of $\Lambda$CDM scenario. Wald-Gauss-Bonnet (WGB) topological dark energy provides a physically motivated realization of this possibility, where the effective dark-energy sector emerges from cosmic horizon thermodynamics and the black-hole formation and merger history. We present the first early- and late-Universe analysis of WGB cosmology, implementing the model as an effective fluid in a modified \texttt{CLASS} solver and constraining it against CMB data from \textit{Planck}, ACT~DR6 and SPT-3G, DESI~DR2 BAO, and Pantheon+ supernovae. While late-time data alone are consistent with $\Lambda$CDM, the full dataset prefers a non-zero WGB contribution, $\Cn=0.387^{+0.118}_{-0.072}$, corresponding to a $>3\sigma$ phantom-like deviation and an improved fit ($\Delta\chi^2=-10.3$). The preferred solution raises $H_0$ from $68.5$ to $69.8~\kmsmpc$, reducing the Hubble tension by $\sim1\sigma$, at the cost of a mild increase in $S_8$. The reconstructed cosmological observables show that WGB leaves the primary CMB almost unchanged while enhancing lensing and small-scale clustering, revealing a characteristic $H_0$-$S_8$ trade-off. WGB dark energy therefore emerges as a physically motivated and observationally viable late-time mechanism for partially alleviating the Hubble tension without introducing new early-Universe physics.

hep-th.title: Prospects for Direct Detection of Ultralight Dark Matter candidates in deci-Hz Band with IndIGO-D
hep-th.author: Md. Emanuel Hoque, Andrew L. Miller, Arunava Mukherjee
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of IndIGO-D, a proposed space-based decihertz gravitational-wave interferometer, to different classes of ultralight dark matter. IndIGO-D will probe the $\sim0.01$--$10~\mathrm{Hz}$ frequency band between those accessible to current ground- and future space-based gravitational-wave interferometers, providing access to ultralight dark-matter masses beyond the reach of existing instruments. We consider two complementary signatures: interferometric displacements induced by coherently oscillating scalar (dilaton), vector (dark-photon, $U(1)_B$ and $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge groups), and tensor fields with masses $m_{\rm DM}\sim10^{-17}$--$10^{-14}~\mathrm{eV}$; and changes in laser polarization induced by pseudoscalar axion dark matter at higher masses, around $m_a\sim10^{-12}~\mathrm{eV}$. For the dilatons, dark photons and tensors, we compute the expected sensitivities using two pipelines -- cross-correlation and BSD excess-power -- assuming L-shaped and triangular interferometer layouts and three representative noise power spectral densities (S1, S2, S3), each for two years of continuous observation. We find that the projected sensitivities agree to within a factor of order unity across the search pipelines and interferometer geometries. In particular, we show that IndIGO-D could open previously unconstrained coupling parameter space for vector and tensor dark matter across $m_{\rm DM}\sim10^{-16}$--$10^{-14}~\mathrm{eV}$, bridging the sensitivity of space- and ground-based experiments. For axion dark matter, we demonstrate that a complementary detection for laser light polarization shifts, limited primarily by photon shot noise, could probe the axion-photon coupling $g_{a\gamma}$ at masses around $m_a\sim10^{-12}~\mathrm{eV}$ at a level potentially better than that of other future experiments without degrading sensitivity to gravitational waves.

hep-th.title: The hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric lattice QCD with twisted-mass fermions
hep-th.author: C. Alexandrou, S. Bacchio, A. De Santis, A. Evangelista, J. Finkenrath, R. Frezzotti, G. Gagliardi, M. Garofalo, N. Kalntis, B. Kostrzewa, V. Lubicz, L. Maio, F. Margari, F. Pittler, S. Romiti, F. Sanfilippo, C. Schneider, S. Simula, N. Tantalo, C. Urbach, U. Wenger(Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration)
hep-th.abstract: We present a lattice-QCD calculation of the leading-order hadronic-vacuum-polarization (HVP) contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in isospin-symmetric QCD. We employ the gauge configurations generated by the Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration (ETMC) with $N_f = 2 + 1 + 1$ flavors of Wilson-clover twisted-mass quarks at four lattice spacings and at values of the quark-mass parameters matching the definition of isospin-symmetric QCD given in the FLAG review 2024 and in the 2025 edition of the Muon $g-2$ Theory Initiative White Paper (WP25). After retuning the simulation parameters to precisely match these two definitions of isospin-symmetric QCD, and after carrying out an extrapolation to the continuum limit based on the data at lattice spacings $a \simeq 0.049, 0.057, 0.068$ and $0.079$~fm, and spatial lattice sizes up to $L \simeq 7.7$~fm, we obtain $a_\mu^{\rm HVP, FLAG}(\rm{iso}) = (720.0 \pm 6.9) \times 10^{-10}$ and $a_\mu^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso}) = (714.8 \pm 7.4) \times 10^{-10}$. Our results, which have a relative uncertainty of about $1 \%$, agree well with the corresponding determinations by other lattice groups. After adding to our determination of $a_{\mu}^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso})$ the leading isospin-breaking corrections provided in the WP25, namely $a_{\mu}^{\rm HVP, WP25}({\rm IB}) = 0.1(3.4)\times 10^{-10}$, we obtain for the full HVP the value $a_{\mu}^{\rm HVP}= (714.9 \pm 8.1)\times 10^{-10}$. This result translates into a Standard Model prediction for the muon anomalous magnetic moment that is fully consistent with the latest result by the Fermilab Muon $g-2$ experiment and strengthens the tension between lattice QCD and data-driven (pre-CMD3) dispersive determinations.

hep-th.title: Double diffraction production for dipole-dipole scattering at high energies
hep-th.author: Carlos Contreras(UTFSM), Jose Garrido(UTFSM), Eugene Levin(Tel Aviv U.)
hep-th.abstract: This paper is a first attempt to describe double diffractive production in dipole-dipole scattering within high energy QCD. Our approach is based on summing large BFKL Pomeron loops, which generate two clusters of hadrons separated by a rapidity gap. Unlike in the BK framework, our approach allows both clusters to carry large masses. We derive the cross section for the production of two such clusters and show that it exhibits geometric scaling. Testing this scaling behaviour against data from high-energy colliders such as the LHC will be a crucial step in establishing whether large Pomeron loops play a major role in high energy QCD dynamics, and in particular in the unitarization of the scattering amplitude.

hep-th.title: Massive Scalar Quasinormal Modes and Quasibound States of Charged Black Holes with Logarithmic corrections
hep-th.author: Prosenjit Paul, Rickmoy Samanta
hep-th.abstract: We study how long-range deformations in a black-hole metric affect the oscillation, trapping, and decay of a neutral, minimally coupled massive scalar field. We choose a logarithmic deformation of Reissner-Nordström (RN) sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics. It provides an exact solution of Einstein gravity and admits a finite completion. The same geometry also arises in a phenomenological perfect-fluid dark-matter model. In this setup, we analyze both quasinormal modes (QNMs), which describe relaxation, and quasibound states (QBSs), which describe trapped modes with small horizon absorption. We first show that a small scalar mass moves the potential barrier outward, raises it, and reduces its curvature. First-order WKB then predicts weaker damping at every fixed finite multipole and overtone. We then compare several approaches, namely sixth-order WKB, global matching, a generalized Leaver method (adapted to the logarithmic geometry) and time-domain evolution. All methods yield consistent QNM estimates within their ranges of validity. Global matching and Leaver also agree closely for QBSs. Further analytic estimates with a reference trapped state show that a local Padé approximation gives a binding-energy error of about $0.04\%$, while leading Gamow tunnelling underestimates damping by about $25\%$. Across the sampled QBSs, increasing the scalar mass or nonlinear coupling strengthens binding but shortens the lifetime through greater horizon absorption. Finally, using an appropriate horizon regularization and a common complex radial contour, we demonstrate orthogonality of an independently computed QNM-QBS pair using a suitable relativistic bilinear framework.

hep-th.title: Nucleon Wave Functions from QCD Vacuum Topology
hep-th.author: Wei-Yang Liu, Ismail Zahed
hep-th.abstract: Instantons, as topologically nontrivial gauge field configurations, provide a microscopic mechanism for chiral symmetry breaking and the $U_A(1)$ anomaly in QCD. Within the instanton liquid model (ILM), instantons generate multi-fermion interactions governed by their density and size. Using this framework, we develop a microscopic description of the nucleon based on instanton-induced quark--quark correlations. We derive the diquark interaction kernels arising from single instantons and instanton--anti-instanton molecules, revealing a strong attraction in the scalar channel and weaker correlations in the spin-one channels. Embedding these interactions in a covariant, permutation-symmetric Bethe--Salpeter--Faddeev equation yields a nucleon mass $m_N=939.53~{\rm MeV}$, with a predominantly scalar-diquark component ($98\%$) and a small axial-vector admixture ($2\%$) around the mass pole. Despite its small weight, the small admixture generates substantial spin--isospin interference, yielding an axial charge $g_A=1.265$, close to experiment. The resulting covariant amplitude is analytically continued to the light front to obtain the leading three-quark wave function. The corresponding unpolarized, helicity, and transversity parton distributions, along with their QCD-evolved moments, provide a direct connection to lattice QCD calculations and global-fit analyses. Our results show that the topology of the QCD vacuum organizes not only the nucleon mass and spin structure, but also its leading valence partonic content, providing a microscopic foundation for a more complete description including confinement and higher Fock components.

hep-th.title: HWF Analysis of TRN Black Holes
hep-th.author: Ashfaque Ahmad, Sudhir Kumar Gupta, Abbas Ali
hep-th.abstract: We extend the horizon wave-function (HWF) formalism to a spherically symmetric, charged, spinless quantum source in $\mathcal{D} + 1$ dimensional spacetime geometry and construct the HWFs associated with inner- as well as outer-horizons of the Tangherlini--Reissner--Nordström (TRN) black hole. The corresponding black hole formation probabilities, $P_{\rm BH}^{\pm}$, are also calculated and their sensitivities due to various source parameters including charge, mass, and $\mathcal{D}$ are analysed as well. Our analysis reveals that the ratio of inner- to outer-horizon probabilities, $P_{\rm BH}^{-}/P_{\rm BH}^{+}$, changes drastically from being unity as the source departs away from being in the extremal limit defined by $\alpha$ ($\to 1$ for extremal case). Furthermore, black hole formation probabilities are found to be highly suppressed for higher values of $\mathcal{D}$, particularly for the source mass, $m \lesssim \Lambda_{\mathcal{D}}$, e.g., for $\alpha = 0.5$, the ratio, $P_{\rm BH}^{+}(\mathcal{D} = 5)/P_{\rm BH}^{+}(\mathcal{D}=10)$ turn out to be approximately $2.95\times10^3$, $117$, and $3.35$ respectively for $m/\Lambda_{\mathcal{D}} = 0.5, 1$ and $2$, with $\Lambda_{\mathcal{D}}$ being the reduced gravity scale associated with $\mathcal{D}$ spatial-dimensions.
